headline: Electric vehicles 33% cheaper to run across EU in 2025
meta_description: New research shows EVs cost significantly less to drive than petrol cars across the European Union, as battery costs continue to fall.
summary_short: Electric vehicles proved 33% cheaper to operate than petrol cars across the EU in 2025, marking a major shift in the economics of transport.
body:
Electric vehicles were 33% cheaper to drive than petrol cars across the European Union in 2025, according to new research from the International Council on Clean Transportation.

The finding reflects a dramatic shift in transport economics. Battery costs, a historic barrier to EV adoption, have continued their downward trajectory, making electric powertrains increasingly accessible to everyday drivers. As production scales and technology improves, the gap between EV and traditional fuel costs widens in favor of cleaner vehicles.

This cost advantage matters most to ordinary families weighing their next car purchase. Lower operating expenses mean EVs move beyond being an environmental choice to becoming a practical financial one—a tipping point that could accelerate Europe's transition away from fossil fuel dependence.
quick_facts: EVs cost 33% less to drive than petrol cars in the EU, 2025
Battery costs continue falling, making EVs more affordable
Research from International Council on Clean Transportation
